events.title: Trinity's capture turns into a massacre
events.summary: Four cops breach Room 303 in the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she raises her hands behind her head in apparent surrender. Outside, the Lieutenant brags that his units are bringing down 'one little girl' while Agent Smith tells him those men are already dead. Back inside, the moment the Big Cop reaches with the cuffs, Trinity moves inhumanly fast: she shatters his nose and hurls him across the room into another cop, killing them both, snatches a gun, twists it, and fires. When the gunfire ends, one flashlight rocks slowly to a stop over the dead and Trinity is the only one standing, unhurt. She lets slip a single 'Shit.' Outside, Smith turns and heads into the hotel on Smith's nod, leaving the defiant, disbelieving Lieutenant behind.
events.action: The raid on Room 303 inverts in a single instant. Trinity's surrender in the room is a choice, not a defeat: she lets the squad believe the arrest is routine, then converts the first physical contact — the Big Cop's cuffs reaching for her — into the opening of her violence. She breaks the perimeter, turns the cops' own momentum and weapons against them, and by the end has wiped out the armed, outnumbering squad, standing alone over the dead as the victor rather than the captive. Outside the hotel, the Agents already know the outcome and move to seize the operation while the Lieutenant, still believing his men are succeeding, rages against them in denial.

state_triples.reading: Her obedience was never defeat; it was the cheaper exit chosen to buy seconds, and the slowness of her surrender was calculation, not fear. She lets the squad see a cornered woman right up to the instant she lets them see a ghost. The trigger for her violence is not threat but touch — the cuff reaching for her — which she converts into the moment she stops being the arrested. The lone 'Shit' afterward is the only crack in a composure that has just killed four armed men.

state_triples.reading: His 'Oh shit' is genuine recognition of the agents, and the bluster that follows — mocking 'Juris-my dick-tion,' telling them to 'cram it up your ass' — is a shield against being made small in front of his own officers. He reads them through the ordinary lens of an inter-agency turf war and cannot conceive that they are right: his men are not succeeding but already dead. His territorial pride is what keeps the police interfering and dying, and his confident posture rests entirely on a reality that no longer exists.

state_triples.reading: Their training gives them no category for something that moves faster than their shared sense of what is possible, so they substitute volume — raking the walls, sweeping lights, firing at motion. They go from the disciplined bead of a controlled arrest to being disarmed and killed inside a few lines, and their panic is legible precisely against the Big Cop's prior certainty. They die believing they outnumbered and outgunned one unarmed woman — the superiority they counted on is exactly what gets them all killed.

events.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
events.summary: Morpheus tells Trinity the traced hardline is cut and she must reach the Wells and Lake phone instead. She bolts through a hall where Agent Brown appears and out a broken window onto the fire escape, only to find Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, forcing her up onto the roof. She runs the rooftops with cold grace while the cops flounder and Brown duplicates her leap across the 40-foot gap, then she dives through a lit window, crashes down a stairwell, and races the garbage truck to the booth. She answers the Wells and Lake phone and is gone before the truck destroys the booth. On the street, the Agents convert the loss into a colder victory: the informant is real and they now have the next target's name.

state_triples.reading: Brown is the event's quiet revelation that the pursuers break the world's rules too: his 'unnatural grace' and his exact duplication of Trinity's leap — landing, rolling, up onto one knee as if mirroring her were obvious — tell the cops and the audience that the Agents are not men bound by physics. state_triples.reading: Smith's is the event's true pivot. His frustration at losing Trinity again is real and bodily — jaw set, grinding his molars — but it flips the instant Brown confirms the informant is real: he almost smiles, and the failure stops mattering because a colder pleasure has arrived. The hunt now has a name. He reads the betrayal as simple loyalty to the system, not yet knowing it is Cypher trading his crew for his own return, and he underestimates the escape he dismisses — Trinity is the one who will reach Neo first.

events.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
events.summary: Alone in his technology-crammed apartment, Neo is jolted from sleep by his own PC typing messages at him that end with a real knock answering the screen, leaving him unable to tell whether he was awake or dreaming. He still closes a disk-for-cash deal with Choi through his chained, multi-locked door, but the visit leaves him hollowed by a returning sense of unrealness, and when Dujour proposes taking him out he refuses until he spots a small white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which the room seems to tilt and he agrees. At a smoke-filled gathering of people dressed in black, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as the hacker who was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless solitude as a search for a hidden figure and an answer no one can be told. Pressing close in the deafening music, she withholds the substance and instead gives him the question, which he finally voices aloud before she melts back into the crowd, leaving him with the promise that the answer is out there and will find him.
events.action: Neo is woken at his PC by messages that type themselves on his screen and end with a knock that answers the last line, cracking his cause-and-effect certainty and blurring the machine into the real. He performs normalcy, opening his series of locks and chain to complete a disk-for-cash deal with Choi, then is left hollowed by a recurring wave of unrealness. He refuses Dujour's offer to go out until the white rabbit pin on her jacket flips him into motion, and he arrives at the party out of place, beer in hand. Trinity approaches, names herself as the one who was on his computer, warns him he is being watched and in danger, and turns his private, sleepless obsession into a directed search, pressing close in the loud music until he voices What is the Matrix? and is told the answer can only be seen, not explained. She then withdraws into the shifting crowd, leaving him alone with the question and the promise that the answer will find him.

state_triples.reading: Neo begins the night as a man who trusts that the world runs on causes he can trace, and by its end he is being steered by a question he cannot yet answer. The messages and the answering knock crack his certainty just enough that a coincidence — a white rabbit pin — can tip him into motion, and he reads both as noise he can joke away rather than as a summons aimed at him. prose_before_reconcile.summary: Alone in his technology-crammed apartment, Neo is woken by his own PC typing messages at him that end with a knock that answers the screen, and he is left unable to explain whether he was awake or dreaming. He still closes a disk-for-cash deal with Choi through the chained door, but the visit leaves him hollowed by a returning sense of unrealness, and when Dujour proposes taking him out he refuses until he spots a white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which the room seems to tilt and he agrees. prose_before_reconcile.action: At a smoke-filled gathering of people dressed in black, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as the hacker who was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless solitude as a search for a hidden figure and an answer no one can be told. Pressing close in the deafening music, she withholds the substance and instead gives him the question, which he finally voices aloud before she melts back into the crowd, leaving him with the promise that the answer is out there and will find him.

events.title: Neo's ordinary life reasserts itself
events.summary: The alarm drags Neo awake at 9:15 A.M. in his own apartment, and he reacts with alarmed cursing at the time. An establishing shot names the destination as the downtown headquarters of Meta CorTechs, a software development firm. There, Rhineheart lectures him without looking up from his computer, accusing him of a problem with authority and demanding conformity as part of a whole, then delivers an ultimatum: be on time from this day forth or find another job. Neo, who has spent the exchange watching the window cleaners outside, answers with crisp deference — 'Yes, Mr. Rhineheart. Perfectly clear.' The vast, destabilizing pull of the night before collapses back into the mundane mechanics of a job he is about to lose.

events.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
events.summary: A softpak delivers a ringing phone to Neo's cubicle and Morpheus guides him through the raid, but the escape stalls at a window ledge and ends when the Agents take him into custody, which Trinity sees from outside.
events.action: A Federal Express Guy delivers a softpak to Neo at his cubicle; inside is a cellular phone that rings the moment Neo holds it, and Morpheus warns that forces are closing in. Neo peeks over the partition and spots Agent Smith, Agent Brown and Agent Jones guiding a cluster of officers, while a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's commands, Neo lunges into the empty cubicle across the hall, hides in a corner while the Agents search his own, then rolls out and sneaks down he moves down the line until he reaches the first office on the left side. Alone in that office, he opens a window onto a scaffold and a ledge, argues that the climb is impossible, then commits and climbs out onto the ledge anyway; a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone and watches it fall, and his nerve breaks so he climbs back inside just as a cop opens the door. Outside the skyscraper, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo through the revolving doors and force him into a dark sedan while Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken in her rearview mirror.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: A phone arrives at Neo's cubicle and Morpheus guides him through the raid that follows, but the escape stalls at a window ledge and ends when the Agents take him into custody, which Trinity sees from outside.
prose_before_reconcile.action: A Federal Express Guy delivers a softpak to Neo at his cubicle; inside is a cellular phone that rings the moment Neo holds it, and Morpheus warns that people are coming for him. Neo peeks over the partition and Neo looks up over the partition to see Agent Smith, Agent Brown and Agent Jones escorting a squad of cops, while a woman indicates his cubicle., while a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's commands, Neo lunges into the empty cubicle across the hall, hides in a corner while the Agents search his own, then rolls out and sneaks down the stretch of cubicles to the first door on his left. Alone in that office, he opens a window onto a scaffold and a ledge, argues that the climb is impossible, then commits and climbs out onto the ledge anyway; a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone and watches it fall, and his nerve breaks so he climbs back inside just as a cop opens the door. Outside the skyscraper, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo through the revolving doors and force him into a dark sedan while Trinity watches in her motorcycle's rearview mirror and reacts with dismay.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Neo's inability to trust and take the ledge — his nerve breaks at the wind and the drop, and he climbs back inside toward the very custody he feared.

events.title: Neo is interrogated and implanted
events.summary: In a white interrogation room, Agent Smith reads Neo the contents of his file and offers to wipe his crimes clean in exchange for Morpheus's location. Neo refuses with contempt, gives Smith the finger, and demands a phone call. When Smith asks what good a call is if he cannot speak, Neo's lips meld together until his mouth is gone. Neo lunges for the door; the standing Agents pin him to the chair and tear open his shirt, and Smith drives a fiber-optic tap that has become a living insect-worm creature into his navel, where it burrows inside him as he panics and struggles.
events.action: The scene opens on Neo seated whole-bodied and defiant in the room. Smith sits across from him, lays down the manila file labeled "Anderson, Thomas A.", and runs through Neo's two lives before offering to wipe the slate clean for Morpheus. Neo rejects the bargain, insults Smith, and demands his phone call. Smith removes his sunglasses to show ice-blue eyes and asks what use a call is if Neo cannot speak; Neo's lips fuse smooth. Neo lunges for the door, the standing Agents seize and hold him down while Smith rips his shirt open, and Smith withdraws a fiber-optic wire that animates into a living creature and drives it into Neo's navel, where it burrows in as Neo struggles helplessly.

His demand for a phone call is a category error, an appeal to rules that do not apply to the being across the table, and the violation that.

events.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
events.summary: Waking from a nightmare that left him mouthless with a creature lodged in his abdomen, Neo is reached by a tapped phone on which Morpheus names him 'the One,' tells him Morpheus has spent his life searching for him, warns that the danger is himself, and wins his reluctant '... Yes' before hanging up. Trinity then pulls up beside him at The Adams Street bridge and gets him into a car, where Switch holds him at gunpoint and the crew means to run a steel-and-glass device on him. Neo tries to bolt, but Trinity's appeal to a road he already knows stops him, and he closes the car door and lets them take him on through the wet dark toward Morpheus — committing without trusting his captors.
events.action: Neo is drawn out of his apartment at NEO'S APARTMENT to the CITY STREET and The Adams Street bridge, then taken into a car and carried onward through the DARK STREET into the custody of Morpheus's crew.

state_triples.reading: Neo moves through the event as a man being named into a fate he never asked for. Each authority — the nightmare, Morpheus, Trinity — promises a future that demands surrender, and every time the promise lands on him as nausea rather than relief because it inverts his belief that he is 'nobody.' His '... Yes' is spoken from vertigo, not conviction, and his final act, closing the car door, is the same reflex dressed up as agency: he chooses the abyss he recognizes over the one he cannot see. He does not yet trust Trinity; he only trusts his own terror a bit

He is correct about the outcome but blind to how little Neo understands or wants any of it; the man on the line agrees from vertigo, and Morpheus mistakes that vertigo for conviction.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Waking from a nightmare that may have been real, Neo is reached by a tapped phone on which Morpheus names him 'the One' and wins his reluctant 'Yes,' sending him to the Adams Street bridge. On the rain-soaked street Trinity pulls up and gets him into a car where Switch holds him at gunpoint and the crew means to run a steel device on him; Neo tries to bolt, but Trinity's appeal to a road he already knows stops him, and he closes the door and lets them take him on into the wet dark. events.title: The Bug Removed
events.summary: In the car rushing through the rainy night, Trinity seals an extractor over Neo's navel and, when suction alone fails to catch the burrowing tracker, overrides his screams and electrocutes him until the fluke-like bug is driven out through the coils. Neo, who had feared only a wire tap, is stunned into belief when he sees the living thing writhing in the glass cage, and Trinity empties it out into the downpour. The car carries them on through the wet night and comes to a halt in the deserted alley behind Hotel Lafayette.
events.action: Trinity fits the extraction device to Neo's stomach and raises the suction while Switch feeds it power from the cigarette lighter; as the ultrasound monitor shows the tracker burrowing and Switch warns it will be lost, Trinity fires an electric charge through Neo, convulsing him until the bug rockets out into the glass cage, which she then empties out the window. The car drives on through the wet night and stops in the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.

events.title: Born Into the Real World
events.summary: Neo tears free of the magenta pod, bald and naked and sight-blurred, and is carried through the body's waste channels after a machine seizes him, unlocks the coaxial cable from the base of his skull, and frees the connective hoses from his limbs and genitals before dropping him into a black hole that vacuums him into the waste line. He slides and nearly drowns in the flow until a metallic cable snatches him up into a flying machine, which carries him into the hovercraft and lowers him, half-conscious, onto its floor. Morpheus names him and the real world, and Neo, emptied by the passage, gives out and collapses.
events.action: A machine disconnects Neo from the pod and the plant, he is flushed through the waste line and nearly drowns, and a flying machine retrieves him and delivers him to the hovercraft, where Morpheus greets him by name before he collapses.

state_triples.reading: Neo is being born rather than merely rescued: he tears out of a womb of gelatin, naked and sight-blurred, and is carried through the body's waste channels before being gathered up by the crew. His collapse is the last act of a self that has been emptied and is not yet refilled.

prose_before_reconcile.action: action: A machine disconnects Neo from the pod and the plant, then a flying machine retrieves him from the waste line and delivers him to the hovercraft, where Morpheus greets him by name before he collapses.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The moment Morpheus names him and the real world is the point the whole extraction has been aiming at: Neo is not simply pulled from the pod but is received and identified, and his collapse answers that welcome rather than the ordeal alone.

events.title: Waking and Rebuilding
events.summary: After Neo is delivered from the machine world onto the hovercraft, Morpheus—certain rather than merely hopeful that they have found the one they sought—oversees his rebuilding on an operating table, where Neo's atrophied muscles are repaired and hardware is grafted into his flesh. Morpheus doles out truth in small doses and finally decides reality must be shown rather than told, so when Neo learns he has lost roughly two centuries (1997 to near 2197) and that the ship is the Nebuchadnezzar, Morpheus leads him, like a sleepwalker, from his room up toward the main deck.
events.action: The crew confirms the rescue; Morpheus shepherds Neo through awakening, physical repair, and reorientation—culminating in the decision to demonstrate the truth instead of describing it—while Trinity voices restraint and Dozer reports on Neo as a body to be rebuilt.

events.title: The Desert of the Real
events.summary: Morpheus leads Neo off the main deck of the Nebuchadnezzar into the Construct and, rather than defining the Matrix in words, jacks him in and shows him. Across the loading program, the televised history of the scorched sky, the fetus fields, and the power plant, Morpheus lays out how humanity was reduced to a grown power source, holding up a coppertop battery as the final proof. Neo refuses every step of it and demands to be let out; back on the main deck his body rejects what he has been shown, and after the cable is pulled he vomits and collapses unconscious.
events.action: The event converts Neo from being told the truth to being forced to survive it — his intellectual refusal becomes a physical one, ending in blackout.

events.title: The Prophecy and the First of the Crew
events.summary: Morpheus answers Neo's grief at there being no return with a myth: he confesses to breaking the rule against freeing older minds, recounts the prophecy of the One and that Zion is the last human city near the earth's core, and declares the search is over before committing Neo to his training. The fluorescent light sticks flicker on, ending the darkness aboard the Nebuchadnezzar. Tank then arrives as Neo's operator, shaking his hand and, when Neo notices the missing jacks, explaining that he and Dozer are born free, genuine children of Zion, before pivoting to the work ahead.
events.action: Morpheus converts Neo's involuntary rescue into a chosen destiny, and Tank gives that destiny a warm human face — together settling a shattered, sleepless man into a recruit being led rather than used.

events.title: The Sparring Program
events.summary: Tank loads combat programs into Neo, skipping the prescribed order for the fun of it, and the download floods Neo with real skill so viscerally that he declares he knows kung fu. Morpheus refuses to celebrate the claim and instead tests it, first explaining in the dojo that the simulation's rules are computer rules that can be bent and broken, then dismantling Neo's furious assault with effortless ease. Beaten and bloodied, Neo blames Morpheus's physical superiority, but Morpheus forces him to see that his speed has nothing to do with muscles and that even the air he breathes is not real. Neo half-accepts this and keeps fighting until rage unlocks a single clean strike that knocks Morpheus's glasses off. Pleased but disciplined, Morpheus reframes himself as only a guide who can show the door, places the responsibility for stepping through on Neo, and orders Tank to load the jump program.
events.action: Tank settles into his operator's chair and loads combat programs into Neo, delighted to skip the boring prescribed order, while the rest of the crew, interrupted at dinner by Mouse's announcement, bolts to the main deck and gathers behind him to watch. Neo, drunk on the downloaded skills, declares he knows kung fu; Morpheus refuses to celebrate it and instead submits it to a test, explaining in the dojo that the simulation's rules are computer rules that can be bent and broken, then dismantling Neo's furious assault with overwhelming force. Beaten and spitting blood, Neo attributes his defeat to Morpheus's physical superiority, but Morpheus forces him to see that his speed has nothing to do with muscles and that even the air he breathes is not real. Neo half-accepts this and keeps fighting until, goaded past hesitation, rage unlocks a single clean strike that knocks Morpheus's glasses off. Pleased but instantly disciplined, Morpheus recasts himself as only a guide who can show the door, insists Neo must step through himself, and orders Tank to load the jump program.

events.title: The Jump
events.summary: The crew relocates from the hovercraft to the main deck to watch on the monitors as Neo attempts the jump. Morpheus demonstrates the leap across the rooftop gap, then instructs Neo to let go of fear, doubt, and disbelief. Neo steels himself and launches but comes up drastically short, plummeting until the ground gives way like a trapeze net. Tank eases the plug out of the injured Neo, who spits blood into his own hand and asks whether death in the Matrix means death in the real world; Morpheus answers that the body cannot live without the mind. Mouse raises the possibility that Neo might succeed, but Switch and Apoc shut down the search for meaning in the failure, and Trinity, having willed Neo across the gap, departs before Cypher's needling reaches her.
events.action: Morpheus crosses the rooftop gap by leaping it, then orders the next exercise and tells Neo to release fear, doubt, and disbelief. Neo runs at the edge, launches, and falls short, plummeting to the ground below. Morpheus helps him up and draws the reason for the failure from him. On the main deck the crew watches the attempt on the screen; Tank eases the plug out of the injured Neo, who spits blood and asks whether death in the Matrix means death in the real world, and Morpheus states the rule that the body cannot live without the mind. Mouse pushes his what-if about Neo succeeding against two dismissals, Switch refuses the failure any meaning, and Trinity, after willing Neo across the gap, leaves before Cypher's remark to her back.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Morpheus demonstrates the jump Neo must make to prove he can free his mind. Neo steel himself and attempts the fifty-foot leap between rooftops but falls short, his disbelief being the cause. He learns the simulation's danger is real, that his mind makes it real and death there kills the body, and is then unplugged, injured, on the main deck.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Morpheus crosses the gap to the far rooftop by leaping it, then instructs Neo to let go of fear, doubt, and disbelief. Neo steels himself and runs at the edge but launches and comes up drastically short, plummeting until the ground gives way like a trapeze net and he comes to rest on his back. Morpheus helps him up and leads him to name the reason for the failure. On the main deck the crew watches the attempt on a screen; afterward Tank eases the plug out of the injured Neo, who spits blood and asks whether death in the Matrix means death in the real world, and Morpheus answers that the body cannot live without the mind.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Neo's recognition that his own disbelief, not his body, is what stopped the jump — the moment he names 'I didn't think I would' as the cause.

events.title: After Hours
events.summary: Trinity comes out of NEO'S ROOM having just had a private moment over Neo that she did not mean anyone to witness, and meets Cypher in the HALL, where his needling about her attachment to Neo reads to her as exposure. She keeps her feelings off the record and answers with doctrine, and Cypher, failing to rattle her, pivots to the Oracle as a way to test Morpheus's certainty. Neo stays only the covered, watched object of the exchange, and Trinity walks away on her own terms while Cypher is left armed with a plan rather than a sneer.
events.action: Trinity steps out of NEO'S ROOM and into the HALL, still recovering from the intimate moment she did not intend to be seen, and finds Cypher watching. He jabs that she never brought him dinner and presses that there is something about Neo, then asks why Morpheus does not take Neo to the Oracle, who would know. She treats him as a cynic to be managed, deflects his suspicion by asking if he is a believer and answering that Morpheus will take Neo when he is ready, and turns away, leaving him behind her.

events.title: The Agent training program
events.summary: In a city street that is revealed to be a training program rather than the Matrix, Morpheus moves through the crowd while Neo is bumped and shouldered off the path. He teaches that Agents are sentient programs who can inhabit anyone still hardwired to the system, and that every human who has fought one has died. When Agent Smith's gun appears, Neo screams in terror, then retreats into skeptical jokes. Morpheus tells him he can become stronger and faster than any Agent, because their strength and speed are bound by rules while his are not, leaving Neo half-believing the promise on authority rather than understanding it.
events.action: Morpheus walks Neo through the frozen street, reclassifying the ordinary people as part of the enemy system and using the woman in the red dress to spring Agent Smith's gun on him. As Neo is jolted by involuntary terror at the gun, Morpheus explains that Agents are sentient programs inhabiting anyone still plugged in, that no one who fought one survived, but that Neo can surpass them because their power is rule-bound while his is not. Neo, who began believing he was inside the real Matrix and confused when it froze, learns this is a training program and that anyone not yet unplugged is potentially an Agent, and ends half-believing the promise that he can exceed an Agent.

events.title: The Sentinel hunt and the ship's hiding
events.summary: A routine check-in on a parallel pipeline turns into an evasion drill when a Sentinel sweeps in on the Nebuchadnezzar. Morpheus orders the ship wedged into a narrow supply line; power is killed and the E.M.P. armed, and the crew waits frozen and freezing while the machine glides over them and passes. Once it disappears, the tension breaks and the ship settles into rest.
events.action: Dozer reports a Squiddy sweeping in and Morpheus orders the ship set down; the Nebuchadnezzar is wedged into a tight pipe. Morpheus hails Tank over the intercom; Tank kills the turbines, confirms power is offline and the E.M.P. armed, and grips the glowing red key. In the darkened cockpit Trinity defines the E.M.P. for Neo, Dozer clears frost from the windshield, Morpheus stops Neo from moving with a warning that the machine will hear him, and the crew watches the machine pass before it disappears. The crew then falls asleep in the hall.

events.title: Cypher's disillusionment and his deal
events.summary: Two scenes, one turn. On the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, Cypher plays the easy veteran for Neo and uses the drink to sour him on Morpheus, confessing his own regret and reframing the prophecy as a repeating body count. He then meets Agent Smith in an upscale restaurant and, no longer conflicted, barters Morpheus for reinsertion into a rich, forgetful life inside the Matrix. The private grumbling of the cockpit becomes an open, named transaction.
events.action: Alone at the operator's chair on the main deck, Cypher is startled by Neo, then pours him Dozer's engine liquor and toasts that he wishes he'd taken the blue pill. He steers the talk to why Neo is here, mocks the 'save the world' mandate as a mindjob, and reveals that Morpheus has already 'found the One' five times before — all of them dead, killed after Morpheus got them believing and each took on an Agent. He tells Neo to run from any Agent, then lets Neo leave for the ladder. Later, in an upscale restaurant, Cypher savors a steak he admits is not real and declares ignorance bliss. He lays out his price to Agent Smith: no memory of his real life, and reinsertion as someone rich and important like an actor. In return he offers his body back to a power plant and whatever Smith wants; Smith names the access codes to the Zion mainframe, and when Cypher says he can't supply them, Smith names the man who can — Morpheus.

state_triples.reading: Cypher wants a co-conspirator in doubt before he wants anything else: by pouring Neo drink after drink and reframing destiny as a body count, he tries to make his own disloyalty feel like shared common sense rather than a solitary secret. He mistakes Neo's awe for the same disillusionment he feels, and that misreading is what lets him walk, unconflicted, into the restaurant. There the regret that has haunted him since he arrived finally buys its comfort — oblivion — and he is at peace with it, because what he cannot bear is not danger but being 'no one'.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Two scenes, one turn. On the main deck, Cypher plays the welcoming crewmate for Neo but uses the cover of a drink to sour Neo on Morpheus, confessing his own regret and reframing the prophecy as a body count. He then meets Agent Smith in a restaurant and, no longer conflicted, barters Morpheus for a rich, forgetful life back inside the Matrix. The private grumbling of the cockpit becomes an open, named transaction.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Cypher starts by startling at Neo's approach, then pours him Dozer's liquor and toasts that he wishes he'd taken the blue pill. He steers the talk to why Neo is here, mocks the 'save the world' mandate as a mindjob, and reveals that Morpheus has already 'found the One' five times — all dead, killed after Morpheus got them believing in bullshit and each took on an Agent. He tells Neo to run from any Agent, then lets Neo leave. Later, in an upscale restaurant, Cypher savors a steak he admits is not real and declares ignorance is bliss. He lays out his price to Agent Smith: no memory of his real life, reinsertion as someone rich and important like an actor. In return he offers his body back to a power plant and whatever Smith wants; Smith names the Zion mainframe access codes, and when Cypher says he can't supply them, Smith names the man who can — Morpheus.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Cypher's regret hardening into an irreversible, named transaction — the moment private disillusionment stops being talk and becomes a deal with the enemy.

events.title: The crew goes in to reach the Oracle
events.summary: After a final ordinary meal, Morpheus singles Neo out to be taken to the Oracle and Tank launches the ship. The crew materializes inside the Matrix at the Hotel Lafayette; moving apart from the group, Cypher drops a connecting phone into a garbage can. In the car across the city, Neo confronts the falseness of his own memories and presses for what the Oracle can tell him about who he is, but Trinity goes mute at the moment she must reveal what she was told, while Cypher drives and lets his contempt for the crew's faith show as a teasing aside.
events.action: The crew transitions from the ship into the Matrix to deliver Neo to the Oracle, while Cypher, having already sold them, rejoins the group and sets the betrayal in motion.

events.title: Entering the building and meeting the Oracle
events.summary: The crew arrives at a vast, tenement-like building and, as they move through it, it is revealed as a place where people can disappear. Morpheus and Neo go up in the elevator and down a dark hall to a door Neo resists; there Morpheus confesses that he misread the Oracle, thought the prophecy was about himself, and lost his way after five dead candidates, so that when the door opens on its own he has only hard-won faith to offer. Inside, the Priestess separates them—Morpheus is left waiting while a boy teaches Neo that there is no spoon, and Neo, having begun to see the spoon and the room bend, is called forward to be seen by the Oracle.
events.action: The crew enters the building and ascends; Neo and Morpheus ride the elevator alone, then walk the hall to the Oracle's door, which opens for Neo before he touches it. events.title: The Trap Springs
events.summary: Fresh from the Oracle's verdict, Neo is carried back to the crew with a secret he is told to keep and a death-prophecy he cannot yet act on. The return to the Hotel Lafayette turns that prophecy physical: a repeated cat, a helicopter that should not be growing louder, and Tank's realization on the main deck that the world has been edited into an ambush. The Matrix is rewritten against them — a hardline severed, windows bricked into walls — and Mouse is cornered and killed while the rest of the crew finds every exit sealed. With the stairwell swarming below and no way out, Morpheus seizes Trinity's traceable phone despite the risk and orders Tank to find a way through the building, converting a closing trap into the first move of an escape.
events.action: The crew leaves the Oracle's apartment and is carried by car to the Hotel Lafayette, then moves up the dark stairwell toward the eighth floor. A repeated cat and a helicopter growing louder than it should trigger the crew's recognition that the Matrix has been changed. On the main deck, Tank reads the edit on his screens and races to warn Mouse, but the hardline has already been cut and the windows of ROOM 1313 are bricked up; Mouse is pinned against the brick by gunfire and killed, his body flatlining. With the stairwell swarming below and every exit gone, Morpheus overrides Trinity's warning, rips off his jacket, and seizes her traceable phone as the one remaining variable, then orders Tank to find a structural drawing of the building fast.

state_triples.reading: She has done her work and stepped away: she loaded Neo with a choice and a warning, then let him walk out to meet them. Neo enters this event insisting he doesn't believe in 'fate crap' and leaves it having watched the world prove otherwise — the cat, the helicopter, the bricked windows. The Oracle told him he controls his own life; the trap is the first place that claim gets tested, and his answer is to take the gun and move. He is still carrying the secret that he is 'not the One,' but the event stops caring about that label and starts treating him as the one who has to choose — which is exactly the person the Oracle was shaping.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus carries the Oracle's news that he will die for Neo, and this event is him beginning to make that true. He never panics; he listens to the building while others talk, and when the trap closes he does the one thing his certainty demands — he takes control of the last variable and turns a tracked phone into a tool, accepting the cost to himself. His faith in Neo, freshly reinforced, is what makes him willing to spend his own freedom; the trap does not shake him, it only gives his conviction somewhere to go.

Cypher is the only one the trap does not surprise. He wanted the Oracle's verdict in the car and was shut down; now he gets a bigger, colder answer — that there is no way out — and he meets it with something close to relief. His flatness is not the despair Morpheus tries to rally; it is the calm of a man who has already decided the crew is lost, and his declaration 'We're trapped' is the first open sign of a resignation that runs deeper than fear of the Agents.

Tank believes he can warn him out; Mouse believes he can still get out. Both are wrong, and the flatline is the event telling the crew — and Neo — that this is no longer a prophecy but a body count.

state_triples.reading: Tank is the event's helpless witness — the one who sees the trap being built on his screens and can do nothing but shout warnings that arrive a half-step too late. His arc is the operator's nightmare: he recognizes the edit, names it, tries to get Mouse out, and then can only watch and say 'No, no, no.' The event ends by giving him his function back — Morpheus orders him to find the drawing — because the only answer to helplessness on the deck is work, and Tank is the one who has to find the way out that no longer exists on the floor they're trapped on.

The others are the crew's collective body temperature: unalarmed one moment, frozen the next at two words — 'deja vu.' They do not think or decide; they react as one, which is how the event marks the shift from a routine extraction to a trap. Their freeze is the visible proof that everyone but Neo and Cypher still believes the world is stable — and that the moment they stop trusting it, the hunt is on.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: While the police sweep the Hotel Lafayette floor by floor, Morpheus is guided by Tank through the building's schematics to a precise spot, and the crew cuts through a wall and drops inside the plumbing stack to vanish from the raid. The Agents, having killed Mouse, relay the targets' floor to the other units, which flood the eighth floor and find only an empty room with a hole in the bathroom wall.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The police begin sweeping the Hotel Lafayette's rotting floors. On the ship, Tank pulls up the building's structural diagram and feeds Morpheus the main wet-wall, then guides him step by step to a target spot. In Room 1313, Agent Smith stands over Mouse's body and reports to his unit; when the line clicks dead, he relays that the targets are on the eighth floor. Agent Brown listens in the stairwell as boots clatter up behind him. Cops flood the eighth floor and sweep Room 808, finding it empty except for a man-sized hole smashed through the bathroom wall. Inside the wall, an unnamed group worms down the grease-black stack pipes, light filling the hole above them.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The man-sized hole in the bathroom wall — the crew's cut into the plumbing stack — is the pivot on which the escape turns: it is the only thing standing between the crew and the sweeping police.
